speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If he agrees with that view, then, perhaps the Ministry of Transport (MOT) can take the lead to work with the Town Councils, and then, prescribe these areas as pedestrian-only areas.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I say this because there is a real-life example in Bukit Batok where an elderly lady, after taking out letters from her letter box, collided with a PMD user, and she had to be warded.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I think there are similar circumstances in other places as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In deciding for a public area to be considered as public path, either shared or pedestrian-only paths, or for exemption under the Active Mobility Act, we do consider three key principles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: One, which is, safety; second, connectivity; and third, clarity of rules.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, in the area of safety, as long as the surface paths are accessible to the public, they will, by default, be allowed for cycling and PMD use, unless there are safety concerns that cannot be effectively mitigated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The second consideration of connectivity is whether the path is critical for connectivity, for example, if the path links a large cycling path network or connects to key transport nodes and public amenities and, if they are, whether there are alternative paths available to be considered.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Thirdly, in implementing these rules, we want to make sure that these areas can be clearly demarcated so that they can be exempted without causing any public confusion.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Void decks can be easily demarcated to avoid any confusion.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This approach provides the Town Councils with the flexibility to set and enforce their own rules on the usage of active mobility devices, according to their own needs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, if the Town Council feels that void decks are areas where potential accidents can happen, then the Town Council can ban the use of PMDs in the void decks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The point is that people in these areas would not be exercising the same caution as crossing roads.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, in those circumstances, would the Ministry consider imposing regulations?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Because I think the interest of residents in this area would be paramount and also, there would be no real difference in opinions of all the Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They all want the ground floor lift lobbies and the letter box areas to be safe for residents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Yes, I agree with Mr Murali Pillai that we do take safety as the top priority.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have brought up this matter many times.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Before the Act came into force, Town Councils and the Police had been taking enforcement actions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But since the Active Mobility Act came into force, we could not take action and residents have been complaining about near-miss accidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I do not want to see anyone injured at my Khatib Centre.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If the Town Councils were to decide the void deck is to be banned from PMD use, then the Town Council can exercise the enforcement action on PMD users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But in areas outside the void deck which are exempted from the Active Mobility Act, yes, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah is correct to say that Town Council employees are not able to carry out enforcement today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: To that extent, it is clear that PMDs can be dangerous at void decks and also when they exit from lift lobbies.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is going to grow in the next 10 years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe that if the Ministry takes the lead, then you will have a lesser chance of untoward incidents happening.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have mentioned before, I think the configuration of void decks differs from one place to another.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Depending on the needs of the Town Council, we allow Town Councils to exercise the flexibility whether to ban or not to ban.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I think at the end of the day, we are cognisant of the fact that safety is paramount.
